// AUTO-GENERATED outer-tiled MX matmul baseline (41x512x512).
// Strategy 1: Reuse B tiles across I-tile iterations by making j0 the outer loop.
void solution(void) {
  // Issue flush and config once before all loops — format never changes.
  gemmini_flush(0);
  gemmini_extended3_config_ex(WEIGHT_STATIONARY, 0, 0, ACC_SCALE_IDENTITY,
                               1, 1, 0, 0, false, 0, 0, 3, 0);

  int tiles_block = BLK / DIM;   // number of DIM-tiles per BLK side
  int tiles_K     = MATMUL_K / DIM;

  uint32_t a_base = 0;
  uint32_t b_base = BANK_NUM * BANK_ROWS - tiles_block * tiles_K * DIM;
  int SPAD_DEST   = 128;

  // j0 is now the OUTER loop: B tiles are loaded once per j0 and reused
  // across all i0 iterations.
  for (int j0 = 0; j0 < BLOCKS_N; j0++) {
    int ncols = REAL_N - j0 * BLK;
    if (ncols <= 0) continue;
    if (ncols > BLK) ncols = BLK;

    // Stage B scales once per j0 (they are the same for every i0 at this j0).
    for (int g = 0; g < MATMUL_K / 32; g++)
      memcpy(&B_s[g][0], &B_scales_col[g][j0 * BLK], BLK);

    // Mvin all B tiles once per j0.
    // B layout in scratchpad: b_base + (k * tiles_block + j) * DIM
    // B DRAM layout: B_in[k*DIM][j0*BLK + j*DIM], stride = MATMUL_N columns.
    // Must use gemmini_extended_mvin (port 0) — loop_ws_spad requires port-0 scratchpad.
    gemmini_config_ld(MATMUL_N * sizeof(elem_t));
    for (int j = 0; j < tiles_block; j++)
      for (int k = 0; k < tiles_K; k++)
        gemmini_extended_mvin(
          (void*)(((elem_t*)B_in) + (k * DIM) * MATMUL_N + (j0 * BLK + j * DIM)),
          b_base + (k * tiles_block + j) * DIM,
          DIM, DIM);

    // i0 is now the INNER loop: A tiles change each iteration; B tiles are fixed.
    for (int i0 = 0; i0 < BLOCKS_M; i0++) {
      int mrows = REAL_M - i0 * BLK;
      if (mrows <= 0) continue;
      if (mrows > BLK) mrows = BLK;

      int pad_i = BLK - mrows;
      int pad_j = BLK - ncols;

      // Stage A scales for this i0 block.
      for (int g = 0; g < MATMUL_K / 32; g++)
        memcpy(&A_s[g][0], &A_scales_row[g][i0 * BLK], BLK);

      // Programming-model sequence per loop_ws_spad invocation:
      // 1. gemmini_extended3_config_ex — already issued once above (format unchanged).
      //    Re-issue only if we need to change strides; format is identical, so skip.
      //    However the ordering rule requires config_ex before mx_load_scales.
      //    Since config_ex was issued at the top (and state persists), we satisfy
      //    the ordering as long as no other config_ex has intervened.

      // 2. Load A and B scales into hardware scale memory.
      gemmini_mx_load_scales((uint64_t)A_s, A_S_BYTES, 0);  // sel=0 → A (activation)
      gemmini_mx_load_scales((uint64_t)B_s, B_S_BYTES, 1);  // sel=1 → B (weight)

      // 3. Mvin A tiles for this i0 block.
      // A layout: a_base + (i * tiles_K + k) * DIM
      // A DRAM layout: A_in[(i0*BLK + i*DIM)][k*DIM], stride = MATMUL_K columns.
      // Must use gemmini_extended_mvin (port 0) — loop_ws_spad requires port-0 scratchpad.
      gemmini_config_ld(MATMUL_K * sizeof(elem_t));
      for (int i = 0; i < tiles_block; i++)
        for (int k = 0; k < tiles_K; k++)
          gemmini_extended_mvin(
            (void*)(((elem_t*)A_in) + (i0 * BLK + i * DIM) * MATMUL_K + k * DIM),
            a_base + (i * tiles_K + k) * DIM,
            DIM, DIM);

      // 4. Configure output stride and requantizer bounds.
      gemmini_config_st(BLK_OUTC * sizeof(out_t));
      gemmini_mxquant_config_mvout((uint64_t)scale_factors,
                                   tiles_block, tiles_block, tiles_K,
                                   0, 0, 1);

      // 5. Execute the fused tiled matmul (one-shot marker re-issued internally
      //    by gemmini_loop_ws_spad via funct 24 + funct 8).
      gemmini_loop_ws_spad(tiles_block, tiles_block, tiles_K,
                           pad_i, pad_j, 0,
                           a_base, BANK_NUM * BANK_ROWS, 0, SPAD_DEST,
                           false, false, false, false, false,
                           NO_ACTIVATION, 0, 0, false, 0x38);

      // 6. Drain BF16 results from mx_smem to DRAM, row by row.
      for (int r = 0; r < mrows; r++)
        gemmini_mx_read_smem(
          &C_hw[i0 * BLK + r][(j0 * BLK) / BF16_PER_WORD],
          SPAD_DEST * 16 + r * BLK,
          ncols);

      // 7. Full memory barrier before host reads output.
      gemmini_fence();
    }
  }
}
